idea.revenue_model: Tuition, with student aid available to eligible students; exact payment mix for this school is not stated.

idea.name: Acquire and professionalize career schools
idea.one_liner: Acquire under-managed proprietary schools, improve their operations, and use them as a platform for growth and further acquisitions.
idea.customer: Owners selling proprietary schools; the acquired schools continue serving career-training students.
idea.offer: Buy schools with established educational programs, then professionalize operations and grow the school group.
idea.revenue_model: Revenue from acquired schools, primarily tuition; the exact mix varies and is not specified for each school.

key_quotes.quote: the way forward, uh, in this space was to look for, um, under-managed, um, solid companies with good educational programming that could be turned around and professionalized.

claims.claim: The regulatory pathway for Jim's acquisition took about five years to work out.
claims.quote: It took us the better part of 5 years to figure out the regulatory pathway

claims.claim: The change-of-ownership rule generally requires a letter of credit equal to 25% of the prior year's Title IV receipts.
claims.quote: Any school that transacts where there's a change in ownership, basically the rule is that you've got to provide 25% of the previous year Title IV receipts.

claims.claim: In a hypothetical example, a school with $1 million in Title IV receipts could need a $250,000 letter of credit.
claims.quote: If you don't meet certain requirements, then you need to post a $250,000 letter of credit.

claims.claim: In a hypothetical example, increasing Title IV receipts from $1 million to $50 million would raise that letter of credit from $250,000 to $12.5 million.
claims.quote: If you take that million dollars and you make that 50 million dollars in title four receipts, all of a sudden that $250,000 becomes 12 million five Yeah.

claims.claim: The letter of credit may tie up capital for about three years before a cure period ends.
claims.quote: that money in the letter of credit generally needs a cure period of, generally speaking, 3 years.

claims.claim: The Porter and Chester transaction required an additional $12 million to $15 million in financing beyond its purchase price.
claims.quote: in the case of, you know, like a Porter and Chester Institute, another 12 or 15 million dollars.

claims.claim: Jim described his purchase amount for the court-reporting school as nominal.
claims.quote: I was able to structure in a way that um, it was um, nominal in terms of the purchase amount

claims.claim: Jim said the acquired court-reporting school was up over 50% after he took it over.
claims.quote: since taking over the school, uh, we're up um, probably over 50%.

claims.claim: Jim described typical sector multiples as three to seven times.
claims.quote: Most of the multiples in our space are generally between, you know, um in terms of cap rates effectively, you know, I'd say three to seven times.

claims.claim: Lenders Jim spoke with were generally comfortable at three to four times debt.
claims.quote: most um folks in the credit markets that I talked to are comfortable at, you know, three to four times.

claims.claim: Jim said sector multiples had reached the tens in the 2000–2010 decade.
claims.quote: multiples were probably pushed up into the 10s for for these businesses.

claims.claim: The school group had about 80% of tuition revenue coming from federal sources.
claims.quote: probably about 80% of the students um in terms of our revenue our tuition revenue are coming from federal sources.

claims.claim: The group had 350 to 400 employees, with about two-thirds in education.
claims.quote: we have um anywhere between, you know, 350 to 400 employees, of which about 2/3 of those um are in the education uh area.

claims.claim: The group had 2,000 to 3,000 students actively taking programs in a given year.
claims.quote: the student counts um generally are ranging between um 2,000 to 3,000 students in a given year that are actively taking our educational programs.

claims.claim: The group saw about 5,000 to 6,000 prospective students per year.
claims.quote: We probably have, you know, 5 6,000 students come prospective students come through our school every year

claims.claim: About half of those prospective students chose to enroll.
claims.quote: of those 5 or 6,000 generally about half of them make decision to to come

claims.claim: Jim reported revenue CAGR of 6% to 7% and EBITDA CAGR of about 10%.
claims.quote: our compound annual growth rate for revenues um 6 7% and our EBITDA uh CAGR is, you know, around 10.

claims.claim: Jim's five-year goal was to more than double the physical footprint and double student count.
claims.quote: in 5 years time, you know, more than double the the physical footprint campus size, double the student count
